rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding ~5 at.% Ti to NbMoTaW, whereas the hidden target adds 20 at.% Re to create an equiatomic NbMoTaWRe film. Both are compositional modifications of the base alloy, but the specific element and amount differ.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions room-temperature mechanical and irradiation testing with helium ions (~20 keV), while the target uses room-temperature deposition, 120 keV He2+ irradiation, and room-temperature nanoindentation/micropillar compression. Both share room-temperature helium irradiation and mechanical testing, but the ion energy and specific test methods differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes Ti segregation to grain boundaries, enhanced dislocation motion, and improved atomic diffusion for self-healing. The target's mechanism relies on Re-induced grain refinement, lattice distortion, excess free volume, and amorphous grain-boundary regions acting as defect sinks to suppress He-bubble growth. Both involve grain-boundary-related defect-sink mechanisms, but the specific structural mediators and pathways differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved room-temperature ductility, fewer irradiation defects, and retained high-temperature strength. The target predicts and observes less irradiation hardening, smaller/more uniform He bubbles, and reduced grain-boundary embrittlement at room temperature, with no high-temperature testing. Both predict improved irradiation resistance relative to NbMoTaW, but the hypothesis adds ductility improvement and high-temperature strength retention, which are not in the target.
